html:
The Khwarazmian Empire was a Persianate Sunni Muslim state, ruled by a dynasty of Turkic slave origin, that grew from the oasis of Khwarazm on the lower Oxus to rule most of Central Asia, Afghanistan and Iran. It lasted from 1077 to 1231.

Its founder was a Turkic slave soldier made governor of Khwarazm by the Seljuks. For a century his descendants were vassals, first of the Seljuks and then of the Qara Khitai. From about 1190 they ruled on their own. Under Shah Muhammad II the empire was the strongest power in the eastern Islamic world: it took Samarkand and Bukhara, defeated the Ghurids, and even threatened the Abbasid caliph in Baghdad. Its army was mostly Kipchak Turkish cavalry.

Its fall was sudden and terrible:

  • 1218: at Otrar, a Khwarazmian governor killed the merchants of a caravan sent by Genghis Khan. The Shah then killed a Mongol envoy.
  • 1219 to 1221: the Mongols invaded. Bukhara, Samarkand, Urgench, Merv, Nishapur and other great cities were taken and many were destroyed, with huge loss of life.
  • 1220 or 1221: Muhammad II died a fugitive on an island in the Caspian.
  • 1221 to 1231: his son Jalal al-Din fought on in India, Iran and the Caucasus until he was killed.

The destruction of Khwarazm was among the bloodiest episodes of the Mongol conquests. It opened the road west for the Mongol Empire.
